bibl.title: Descent for sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Specifically, given a compactly assembled ∞-category ℰ, we show that the functor sending a locally compact Hausdorff space 𝑋 to the ∞-category Shpost(𝑋; ℰ) of Postnikov complete ℰ-valued sheaves on 𝑋 satisfies descent for proper surjections.

span.label: descent for sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces
span.quote: The first goal of these notes is to explain some descent results for ∞-categories of sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces.

span.label: mathematical-proof
span.quote: Section 2 proves Theorem 0.5 and derives some consequences in shape theory.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Descent fails because every compact Hausdorff space is covered by a profinite set, and sheaves on profinite sets are already Postnikov complete while sheaves on a general compact Hausdorff space are not, so the target of the limit is forced to satisfy a completeness the source lacks.
span.quote: The reason for this failure of descent is that every compact Hausdorff space admits a surjection from a profinite set, and the ∞-category of sheaves on a profinite set satisfies a strong completeness property which the ∞-category of (hyper)sheaves on a general compact Hausdorff space does not satisfy.

span.label: The descent and full-faithfulness results fail before Postnikov completion; the paper devotes sections to explaining why.
span.quote: We conclude by explaining why Corollary 4.11 is generally false before passing to Postnikov completions.

span.label: Whether every-object-is-the-limit-of-its-Postnikov-tower is strictly weaker than Postnikov completeness is left open.
span.quote: As far as we are aware, it is not known if there exists an ∞-topos 𝒳 such that every object of 𝒳 is the limit of its Postnikov tower, but 𝒳 is not Postnikov complete.

span.label: The protruncated shape, one of the derived consequences, does not preserve pullbacks.
span.quote: The protruncated shape does not preserve pullbacks of compact Hausdorff spaces.

span.label: Three competing sheaf theories agree on all truncated objects, so which one a result used is invisible until unbounded objects are involved.
span.quote: They all have the same truncated objects, so the subtle differences between these theories only appears when considering

span.label: Two incompatible set-theoretic foundations are in use in this literature; the difference is declared inessential and then not mentioned again.
span.quote: Clausen and Scholze [23] use alternative set-theoretic foundations that avoid using universes. This minor difference is only in the set theory and does not affect any arguments in an essential way, so we will not mention it again

span.label: The agreement between three cohomology theories is claimed for spaces satisfying a stated structural condition, not in general.
span.quote: As a consequence, the condensed, singular, and sheaf cohomologies of a topological space admitting a locally finite CW structure all agree

span.label: sheaf theory - THREE OF THEM, DISTINGUISHED ONLY OFF THE TRUNCATED PART: sheaves, hypersheaves and Postnikov complete sheaves all extend the classical theory and share their truncated objects, so the choice between them is undetectable in the bounded case
span.quote: (sheaves, hypersheaves, and Postnikov complete sheaves) extending the classical theory of sheaves on a topological space

span.label: the subject's name - CONDENSED/PYKNOTIC, BOTH CARRIED: the field is written with a slash between two names for it, in a paper by one of the pyknotic authors thanking the condensed ones
span.quote: We imagine that the reader might be interested in condensed/pyknotic mathematics but not necessarily familiar with all of the intricacies about the theory of ∞-topoi

span.label: the set theory - A DIFFERENCE DECLARED AND THEN SET ASIDE: universes here, no universes there, and an explicit decision not to mention it again
span.quote: This minor difference is only in the set theory and does not affect any arguments in an essential way, so we will not mention it again

span.label: extends → Dyckhoff [7, Theorem 3.11; 8] and Clausen–Scholze [23, Theorem 3.2] comparison of sheaf and condensed cohomology
span.quote: We extend this result in two directions: to locally compact Hausdorff spaces and to very general coefficients.

span.label: builds-on → Clausen–Scholze's condensed/pyknotic mathematics, Barwick–Haine, and Lurie's work on ultracategories
span.quote: Our motivation comes from condensed/pyknotic mathematics developed by Clausen–Scholze [20; 21; 22; 23], in our joint work with Barwick [2, Chapter 13; 3], and in Lurie’s work on ultracategories [17; 18, Chapter 4].

span.label: Postnikov complete sheaves —distinct-from→ hypersheaves
span.quote: (sheaves, hypersheaves, and Postnikov complete sheaves) extending the classical theory of sheaves on a topological space. They all have the same truncated objects, so the subtle differences between these theories only appears when considering

span.label: For a compactly assembled coefficient ∞-category, the assignment of the ∞-category of Postnikov complete sheaves to a locally compact Hausdorff space satisfies descent along proper surjections.
span.quote: Specifically, given a compactly assembled ∞-category ℰ, we show that the functor sending a locally compact Hausdorff space 𝑋 to the ∞-category Shpost(𝑋; ℰ) of Postnikov complete ℰ-valued sheaves on 𝑋 satisfies descent for proper surjections.

span.label: The same result gives proper descent for left complete derived ∞-categories and shows that Postnikov complete sheaves form a sheaf on compact Hausdorff spaces for the topology of finite jointly surjective families.
span.quote: This implies proper descent for left complete derived ∞-categories and that the functor Shpost(−; ℰ) is a sheaf on the category of compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with the topology of finite jointly surjective families.

span.label: Neither ordinary sheaves nor hypersheaves define a sheaf of ∞-topoi on the site of compact Hausdorff spaces, so the descent statement genuinely fails without Postnikov completion.
span.quote: The presheaves Sh, Shhyp ∶ Comp op → LTop∞ are not sheaves.

span.label: Postnikov complete sheaves on a locally compact Hausdorff space embed fully faithfully into condensed objects over that space.
span.quote: Then the pullback functor 𝑐∗,post ∶ Shpost(𝑋; ℰ) → Shpost(Comp∕𝑋; ℰ) is fully faithful.

span.label: Consequently the sheaf cohomology and the condensed cohomology of a locally compact Hausdorff space coincide.
span.quote: This implies that the condensed and sheaf cohomologies of a locally compact Hausdorff space agree.

span.label: For a space carrying a locally finite CW structure, condensed, singular and sheaf cohomology all coincide.
span.quote: As a consequence, the condensed, singular, and sheaf cohomologies of a topological space admitting a locally finite CW structure all agree

span.label: Sheaves on a profinite set are Postnikov complete, whereas sheaves on the Hilbert cube are not, so Postnikov completeness is not automatic for compact Hausdorff spaces.
span.quote: The ∞-topos of sheaves on a profinite set is Postnikov complete. On the other hand, the ∞-topos of sheaves on the Hilbert cube [0, 1] is not Postnikov complete.

span.label: The protruncated shape functor on compact Hausdorff spaces fails to preserve pullbacks, even though it preserves finite coproducts, cofiltered limits and Čech-nerve realizations.
span.quote: The protruncated shape does not preserve pullbacks of compact Hausdorff spaces.

span.label: Postnikov completion of an ∞-topos
span.quote: Let 𝒳 be an ∞-topos. The Postnikov completion of 𝒳 is the limit

span.label: Postnikov complete ∞-topos
span.quote: We say that an ∞-topos 𝒳 is Postnikov complete if the functor 𝑡∗ ∶ 𝒳 → 𝒳post is an equivalence of ∞-categories.

span.label: proper descent (for a functor on locally compact Hausdorff spaces)
span.term: proper descent (for a functor on locally compact Hausdorff spaces)
span.quote: descent if for every proper surjection of locally compact Hausdorff spaces 𝑝 ∶ 𝑋 ↠ 𝑌, the augmented cosimplicial diagram

span.label: compactly assembled ∞-category
span.quote: A presentable ∞-category ℰ is compactly assembled if ℰ is a retract of a compactly generated ∞-category

span.label: hypercomplete objects of an ∞-topos
span.quote: The ∞-category of hypercomplete objects of 𝒳 is the full subcategory 𝒳hyp ⊂ 𝒳 spanned by those objects that are local with respect to the ∞-connected morphisms.

span.label: van Kampen colimit
span.quote: A colimit in an ∞-category 𝒳 with pullbacks is van Kampen if the functor 𝒳op → Cat∞ given by 𝑈 ↦ 𝒳∕𝑈 transforms it into a limit in Cat∞.

span.label: Postnikov complete sheaves
span.quote: We refer to objects of Shpost(𝒞; ℰ) as Postnikov complete sheaves on 𝒞.
